topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and context for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Overview and core principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of the complement system, including its general roles, naming conventions, and the central role of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct pathways that initiate complement activation and converge to reach the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector processes through which complement eliminates pathogens via opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host cells from complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes associated with deficiencies in various complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and applications of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic covers the strategies pathogens use to circumvent complement and the practical laboratory and medical applications derived from evasion proteins.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the closing remarks and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
